subject: Stratify MAP: private deployment evaluation — roles & networking owners
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lewis <sophie@stratify.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stratify MAP: private deployment evaluation — roles & networking owners

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the time this morning. As discussed, I’ve pulled together a lightweight mutual action plan (attached) to align stakeholders and get the Private/VPC evaluation moving. High-level goal: complete a 4-week on-prem / VPC evaluation that proves parity with your latency and security requirements, and surfaces any topology work ahead of procurement.

What I’ve attached:
- Stratify_MAP_v1.xlsx — proposed milestones, owners, success criteria, and target close date (we put a tentative finish on 2027-07-28).
- proposed-network-sketch.png — very rough of VPN termination options (customer VPN -> cloud NW -> private instances).

Immediate asks (can you confirm by EOD Thursday?):
- Who is your primary networking/VPN owner for the evaluation (name + email)?
- Who owns key management / KMS responsibilities (rotation, HSM/KMS provider)?
- Any hard blackout windows for the next 4 weeks we should avoid scheduling tests?

Internal owners from our side (cc’ed):
- Marcus Lin — lead systems engineer (will own network integration & performance testing)
- Neha Kapoor — security/compliance lead (KMS, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts)
- Aditya Rao — solutions engineer (deployment runbook & automation)

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick 30-min sync to lock owners and timeline — can we do Fri Jul 2 or Mon Jul 5?
2) We’ll finalize the MAP and share an updated spreadsheet after the call.
3) Marcus will draft a runbook for VPN termination options so you can pick the preferred topology.

Attaching the MAP as a starting point so you can add or edit owners directly. If you want, Marcus can join your internal infra thread next week.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

—Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Stratify_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), proposed-network-sketch.png (image)
From: Sophie Lewis <sophie@stratify.io>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos@stratify.io>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 20:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Stratify MAP: private deployment evaluation — roles & networking owners

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks — this looks like a good starting point. Quick answers:
- Networking/VPN owner: Carlos Mendes (carlos@stratify.io), infra lead. He’ll own VPN termination and peering decisions.
- KMS owner: I’m the business owner but we’ll have Sanjay Patel (sanjay@stratify.io) from security own the KMS config and key rotation policy.
- No blackout windows until mid-July; we do have a compliance review on 2027-07-12 so avoid heavy config changes that day.

We’re aligned on the 4-week evaluation in principle but would like the kickoff call on Fri Jul 2 at 11:00am PT if possible (our engineers prefer a blocker before the weekend). Can Marcus and Neha join? Also a few quick questions for the call so we can prep:
1) For VPN termination — do you support both site-to-site IPsec and client-based tunnels for testing?
2) For KMS — does Redwood integrate with AWS KMS and can you support customer-managed CMKs/HSM?
3) What telemetry will you need from our side during the perf runs? (packet captures, cloudwatch, traceroute, etc.)

If Marcus can share the preliminary runbook ahead of the call that would be great.

—Sophie
Director, Platform Engineering, Stratify Analytics
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Stratify MAP: private deployment evaluation — roles & networking owners

Team — forwarding Sophie's reply so we can lock owners and prep the runbook. Action items:

Marcus — primary for VPN/networking. Please prepare a 1-page runbook that includes: supported termination modes (IPsec site-to-site, client tunnel options), required firewall/NAT rules, expected ports, and an initial checklist for throughput tests. Aim to post to the MAP folder by EOD Thu (2027-07-01).

Neha — primary for KMS/security. Confirm Redwood’s integration story with AWS KMS / customer-managed keys and whether HSM-backed keys are supported. Also list the audit logs / traces we’ll surface to Stratify for the evaluation. Sanjay (Stratify) will be the point on their side.

Aditya — draft the experiment plan for week 2 perf runs (test vectors, traffic profiles, success thresholds).

I’ll schedule the 30-min kickoff for Fri Jul 2, 11:00am PT and invite Sophie, Carlos, and Sanjay. If any of you cannot make that time, flag now.

Keep the replies internal for now — I’ll loop in the external team only once we have the runbook and a clean MAP.

—Stephanie
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lewis <sophie@stratify.io>, Carlos Mendes <carlos@stratify.io>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay@stratify.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stratify MAP: private deployment evaluation — roles & networking owners

Hi Sophie / Carlos / Sanjay —

Thanks for the quick responses and for confirming owners. We’ve scheduled the kickoff:
- When: Fri Jul 2, 2027, 11:00am PT (Calendar invite sent)
- Who from Redwood: Marcus (networking), Neha (security), Aditya (solutions)
- Who from Stratify: Sophie (business), Carlos (infra), Sanjay (security)

Answers to your prep questions (short):
1) VPN modes: We support site-to-site IPsec and client-based tunnels for validation; Marcus will enumerate the recommended approach for throughput tests.
2) KMS: Redwood integrates with AWS KMS and supports customer-managed CMKs. HSM-backed keys are supported for Private deployments with an enterprise key store — Neha will share exact config notes.
3) Telemetry: packet captures and traceroutes are useful for initial diagnostics; we’ll ask for cloud metrics (CPU, network util) plus any internal request traces you can share.

We’ve uploaded an updated MAP and a draft network runbook to the shared Drive link included below; Marcus will send a condensed one-pager before the call so you have something to react to.

Shared materials: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMAPfolder

See you Friday —

—Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai
